name: @slack/radar-mcp

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Check if Slack Radar is running. Returns uptime, buffer sizes, remaining session time, stream status, the Radar MCP tool version (mcp_version), and which app/profile is bound: android_user_id (0 = personal, non-zero = a secondary user such as a work profile), profile ('personal'/'secondary'), and package.

timeout_minutes.description: Set or extend the auto-shutdown timeout in minutes (default: 5).

tools.name: get_recent_network_calls
tools.description: Get recent HTTP network calls captured from the Slack Android app.

limit.description: Max number of calls to return (default: 50)

tools.name: get_network_call_detail
tools.description: Get full details of a specific network call by ID, including request/response headers and bodies.

tools.name: get_recent_rtm_events
tools.description: Get recent RTM (Real Time Messaging) event summaries.

limit.description: Max number of events to return (default: 50)

tools.name: get_rtm_event_detail
tools.description: Get full details of a specific RTM event by ID, including the complete JSON payload.

tools.name: get_recent_clogs
tools.description: Get recent clog (analytics) event summaries. Returns event name and timestamp. Use get_clog_detail for the full JSON payload.

limit.description: Max number of clogs to return (default: 50)

tools.name: get_clog_detail
tools.description: Get full details of a specific clog event by ID, including the complete JSON payload.

tools.name: get_recent_traces
tools.description: Get recent performance trace summaries (one row per completed span from the app's telemetry pipeline). Returns trace name, span name, and duration. Use get_trace_detail for the full span, including its tags and the parent/trace ids.

limit.description: Max number of traces to return (default: 50)

name.description: Filter by trace name or span name substring

tools.name: get_trace_detail
tools.description: Get full details of a specific performance trace by ID: trace and span names, the trace and parent ids, start/end/duration, and the span tags.

tools.name: wait_for_events
tools.description: Wait for matching events to arrive in real-time via the SSE stream.

event_type.description: RTM event type to wait for

source.description: Limit to one stream: network, rtm, clog, log, or trace (default: all)

timeout_ms.description: Max time to wait in ms (default: 30000)

idle_timeout_ms.description: Resolve after this many ms of silence (default: 3000)

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search across all captured network calls, RTM events, clogs, and performance traces.

tools.name: get_app_state
tools.description: Get the current app state from the device.

tools.name: get_recent_logs
tools.description: Get recent device logs for the Slack debug build. Reads the app's own log buffer first (the DEBUG-and-above Timber lines the in-app Log Viewer shows, this app only), and falls back to an adb logcat snapshot when that buffer cannot be read. The result includes a `source` field (app_buffer / logcat_capture / logcat_ring) so you can tell a real empty result from a fallback. Leave `tag` out to get all recent lines. For native crashes, VERBOSE lines, or non-Slack processes, use adb logcat directly.

tag.description: Optional substring to filter log lines by (matched anywhere in the line, not an exact tag-column match). Omit to return all recent lines.

limit.description: Max number of lines to return (default: 50, capped at 1000)

grep.description: Optional text to grep within the filtered output

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List Android user profiles that have the Slack debug build running. Use this before activate_for_user when the user asks to switch profiles (personal vs a secondary user such as a work profile) or when logs/app state seem to point at the wrong profile. Returns each profile's userId (e.g. '0' for personal, '10' for a secondary user) and a human label.

tools.name: activate_for_user
tools.description: Activate Slack Radar on a specific Android user profile. Use after list_profiles to switch between the personal user and a secondary user (such as a work profile). Switching profiles restarts log capture with a new session-scoped file and reconnects the SSE event stream so events come from the newly activated profile; old captures remain on disk for up to 7 days. Call this when already connected and only the target profile needs to change.

user_id.description: Android user ID from list_profiles (e.g. '0' for personal, '10' for a secondary user).

tools.name: capture_snapshot
tools.description: Bundle the current Radar state into a single on-disk artifact for sharing. Writes four files to ~/.slack-radar/snapshots/snapshot-<ts>/: bundle.json (network + RTM + clog + trace buffers, up to 1000 items each — a bulk export, much larger than point queries like get_network_call_detail), logcat.tail.log (last N lines of the active capture), screenshot.png (current screen), and README.txt (receiver-facing explainer). Use when the user says 'save this', 'file this as a bug', 'share this', 'bundle this up', 'attach to a ticket', 'make me a repro', or otherwise wants a shareable reproducible handoff. PRIVACY: bundle.json contains raw API request/response bodies including auth headers, RTM message content, user/team/channel IDs, clog payloads, and performance trace spans — review before sharing externally.

include_logs.description: Include last N lines of the active logcat capture (default: true). No-op when no capture is active.

include_screenshot.description: Include a current screenshot (default: true). Requires a connected device.

log_tail_lines.description: How many trailing lines of the capture file to include (default: 500, min: 1, max: 10000). Truncation flagged in counts.log_lines_truncated.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot from the connected Android device.

tools.name: record_screen
tools.description: Record a short screen video from the connected Android device.

tools.name: clear_buffers
tools.description: Clear all captured network calls and RTM events from both device and local buffers.

tools.name: _radar_session_enable
tools.description: Enable Slack Radar for this session. Sets up ADB forwarding, activates the device-side server, and connects the SSE stream. Called by /radar-enable skill.

device_serial.description: Target device serial from adb devices. Optional; auto-selected when exactly one device is attached. When multiple devices are attached the enable fails with the list; retry with one of the listed serials.

tools.name: _radar_session_disable
tools.description: Disable Slack Radar for this session. Tears down the SSE stream and clears local buffers. Called by /radar-disable skill.

tools.name: open_radar_dashboard
tools.description: Build or refine a custom live dashboard tab in the Slack Radar web UI from a spec YOU author. Suggest this when the user describes a live view the pre-built tabs (Live/Network/RTM/Clogs/Traces/Logs) do not cover (e.g. 'graph calls per second vs response time and flag slow ones', 'beep when I get a DM'); invoke it once they agree. Translate the request into the spec fields below and call this tool; it ensures the web dashboard is running (default http://localhost:8100) and renders your spec as a 'Custom' tab, then returns the URL to share. Calling again replaces/refines it. Does not open a browser window for the user. The dashboard reads a connected device, so Radar must be armed to show data (the dashboard has its own Reconnect button). Debug builds only, local only.

title.description: Short 1-3 word dashboard title; also the Custom tab label.

summary.description: ONE honest plain-English line describing what this shows, including any active filter.

source.description: Which device stream to read. 'all' is a unified timeline mixing network, RTM, clog, trace, and log.

match.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on SUMMARY fields, keyed by source. network: url/method/status_code; rtm: event_type/direction/channel; clog: event_name; trace: trace_name/span_name; log: tag/level/package. NEVER invent a field (a match on an absent field silently matches nothing). For body text use bodyContains instead; for a log level floor use minLevel, not match.level.

bodyContains.description: network/all only: keep calls whose request/response BODY contains this substring (fetches each call's detail).

minLevel.description: log/all only: show log lines at this level or above (WARN keeps WARN, ERROR and FATAL). Rows of other kinds are unaffected. Omit to show every line; VERBOSE means the same and is stored as omitted.

viz.description: Widgets to compose. 'graph' requires a series array.

rateWindowSec.description: Sliding window in seconds for the rate widget (default 10).

field.description: Required for the 'avg' metric, e.g. duration_ms.

extract.description: Pull CONTENT from a record body into the feed: {parse:'response_body'|'request_body'|'data', field:'dot.path', label}.

highlight.description: Flag feed rows whose numeric field breaches a threshold: {field, op:'>'|'>='|'<'|'<='|'==', value, label}.

alert.description: Sentry mode: {sound, flash, say, at}. 'at':N fires once when the match count reaches N; omit to fire on every match.

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: List the app's on-device SQLite databases (the message store, telemetry, etc.) for the bound profile.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the tables (with row counts) in one on-device database. Pass a name from list_databases.

refresh.description: Re-pull a fresh copy from the device instead of reusing the cached pull (default false)

tools.name: query_database
tools.description: Run a read-only SQL query against an on-device database and get the rows back. SELECT/PRAGMA/WITH only (writes and file access are blocked). Use it to answer 'is this row actually in the DB?' during a debug session. Results are capped by row count and total size (the store is plaintext PII); when trimmed the response sets truncated:true with total_rows, so narrow with WHERE/LIMIT and avoid group_concat/blob dumps.

sql.description: A single read-only statement (SELECT, WITH, PRAGMA, EXPLAIN)

refresh.description: Re-pull a fresh copy from the device before querying (default false reuses this session's cached pull)

tools.name: query_session
tools.description: Read the whole current Radar session from the host event spool (every network/RTM/clog/trace frame captured since radar was enabled), filtered and byte-capped so it cannot flood the model context. Covers network/rtm/clog/trace; device logs are not the spool's primary source, use get_recent_logs for those. Use it for 'everything since I enabled', 'the whole session', or 'what did I miss': the get_recent_* tools read the device rings, which drop the oldest events on a long session, while the spool keeps the full session record. A list read (no id) returns SUMMARY fields for network/RTM/trace and full clog records inline. An id read returns the FULL record: for network/RTM/trace the body (request/response, headers, full payload) is pulled from the device on first open and cached in the spool, so a later id read of the same record is served from the file with no device round-trip; clog is already the full record inline. If the body cannot be pulled (device offline, aged out of the ring, or a single body over the byte budget) the id read falls back to the summary with a note. Frames come back newest-first; when truncated:true the result carries an opaque cursor STRING token, which you pass back verbatim as cursor to page strictly older across all sources. Do not build or change the token; it is not an id and not a count. A token from before a spool rotation or a re-enable is rejected with a note (bounded; a normal session never rotates), and you start paging from the newest page again. Pass id (optionally with source) to fetch one whole record by id regardless of age. Ids are per-source, so an unsourced id can match more than one ring; pass source to disambiguate, and the returned frame type tells you which ring answered. A list read scoped to a plain source (source network) returns summaries; to list cached full bodies for a source, scope to its detail tag (source network_detail). An unscoped list read and an id read already prefer the cached full body. When id is set, all filters except source are ignored. Returns an empty result with a note when no spool exists (radar not enabled).

source.description: Opaque frame type tag to match, e.g. network, rtm, clog, trace (or a future source). Matched exactly, not enumerated.

id.description: Return the single whole frame with this id, bypassing the newest-first byte budget. Optionally scope with source. id addresses one record and is unrelated to cursor; there is no older-than-id filter, page with cursor instead.

cursor.description: An OPAQUE paging token returned by a prior truncated result; pass it back verbatim to get the next older page across all sources. It is NOT an event id and NOT a count; do not construct or modify it. A token from before a spool rotation or a re-enable is rejected with a note, and you start paging from the newest page again.

url_filter.description: Keep frames whose url contains this substring.

status_code.description: Keep frames with this exact HTTP status code.

event_type.description: Keep frames with this exact event_type (RTM).

channel.description: Keep frames with this exact channel id (RTM).

name.description: Keep frames whose name contains this substring (clog/trace).

text.description: Keep frames whose serialized JSON contains this substring anywhere (searches the whole frame, including clog detail).

limit.description: Max frames to return; newest kept first.

byte_cap.description: Max serialized output bytes. Defaults to and is hard-capped at the response budget; a larger value is clamped down.

tools.name: list_prefs
tools.description: List the app's SharedPreferences XML files (including feature-flag files like debug_features_*.xml, which holds manual overrides, and easy_features_*.xml, the persisted server snapshot), with file sizes and the Android user they were read from.

user.description: Android user ID to read (0=personal, 10+=work profile). If omitted, uses the first available user.

tools.name: get_prefs
tools.description: Read a SharedPreferences file, parse it, and return its entries (key, type, value). When keys are provided, filter to those keys only (exact match). Reads the on-disk XML, which can lag the app's live in-memory state by the async-write window, so a value may be slightly stale. debug_features_* holds manual overrides only -- a flag absent there means no override was set, not that the flag is off. easy_features_*/feature_flags_* is the persisted server snapshot, not an override list -- a hit there is the server's value, still subject to the same write-lag caveat.

user.description: Android user ID (0=personal, 10+=work profile). If omitted, uses the first available user.

keys.description: If provided, filter results to only these keys (exact match). Omit to return all entries.

tools.name: search_prefs
tools.description: Search SharedPreferences across all files for a user. Performs case-insensitive substring search on key names and stringified values. Returns per-file match results. Reads the on-disk XML, which can lag the app's live in-memory state by the async-write window, so a value may be slightly stale. A hit in debug_features_* is a manual override -- no hit means no override, not that the flag is off. A hit in easy_features_*/feature_flags_* is the server's persisted value, not an override.

user.description: Android user ID (0=personal, 10+=work profile). If omitted, uses the first available user.

tools.name: list_feature_flags
tools.description: List every feature flag the app knows about right now, with its EFFECTIVE value (local override if set, else the server value) and whether that value is a local override. One key appears once per scope and once per signed-in org, each row carrying its own value (plus an org_id on authenticated rows, when the device build reports one), so total_rows counts rows while total_flags counts distinct flags. This is the actual live state the app is using, unlike get_prefs/search_prefs on debug_features_*.xml, which shows only manual overrides. Requires a debug build with the feature-flag Radar plugin; older builds report a clear error instead of the list.

overridden.description: If true, return only flags with a local override active. If false, return only flags with no override (server value in effect). Omit for the complete list.

tools.name: search_feature_flags
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search on feature flag names, against the same live effective-value list as list_feature_flags. One key can match several rows, one per scope and per signed-in org, so matched_rows counts rows and matched_flags counts distinct flags. Use this instead of search_prefs when you need to know whether a flag is actually ON right now, not just whether it has a manual override.

query.description: Search substring, matched against the flag key (case-insensitive).

tools.name: get_feature_flag
tools.description: Look up one feature flag by its exact key (case-sensitive) and return its effective value and override status. Always returns rows: an array, because one key resolves along two axes. Scope (authenticated = the value for a signed-in user, unauthenticated = a visitor who has not signed in yet), and org: each signed-in workspace resolves its own value, so a flag can be ON in one workspace and OFF in another and each gets its own row with an org_id. A bare lookup returns one row per (scope, org), so read every row rather than the first one, and pass scope and/or org_id to narrow. On builds that report it, rows also carry timestamp, the device clock when that row was written, which tells an older row from a newer one. Use list_feature_flags or search_feature_flags first if you are not sure of the exact key.

scope.description: Optional. 'authenticated' (signed-in user) or 'unauthenticated' (visitor). Omit to get rows for every scope that exists.

org_id.description: Optional. Narrow to one signed-in workspace, using the org_id from an earlier row. Omit to get a row per org.

instructions:
Slack Radar provides on-device debugging tools for the Slack Android app via ADB.

SESSION STATE:
Radar starts DISABLED each session. All tools except ping return an error until enabled.
Use /radar-enable to activate, /radar-disable to deactivate.

AUTO-ENABLE: When the user asks an obvious device question, invoke the Skill tool with
skill="radar-enable" FIRST, then proceed with the radar tool call. No need to ask.
Obvious device questions include: clogs, network calls, RTM events, screenshots,
app state, device logs, or any reference to what is happening on the connected device.

TIMEOUT: The device-side radar auto-shuts down after idle. On tool call failure,
the session flips to disabled. Tell the user and offer to re-enable.

When to use:
- "what am I looking at" / "what screen is this" -> screenshot
- "what just happened" / "what's going on" -> get_recent_network_calls + get_recent_rtm_events
- "why isn't this loading" / "this is broken" -> screenshot + get_recent_network_calls(status_code=400 or 500)
- "watch what happens when I..." -> clear_buffers then wait_for_events (DO NOT filter unless the user specifies a type)
- "did that clog fire" / "check analytics" -> get_recent_clogs(name="...")
- "why is this slow" / "how long did X take" / "show me the traces" / "check performance" -> get_recent_traces(name="...") then get_trace_detail
- "what API call was that" -> get_recent_network_calls then get_network_call_detail
- "did I get X" / "did X happen" -> search(query="X") across ALL buffers, not just one
- "everything since I enabled" / "the whole session" / "what did I miss" -> query_session
- "check the debug logs" -> get_recent_logs (tag is OPTIONAL: pass tag="FKDebug" to filter, or omit it for all recent lines)
- "is flag X on?" / "what is the effective value of X" / "what feature flags does the app have" -> get_feature_flag(key="X") / search_feature_flags(query="X") / list_feature_flags. This is the LIVE effective state (override if set, else server value), requires a debug build with the feature-flag Radar plugin.
- "what feature-flag overrides are set?" / "check debug_features" -> search_prefs(query="X") or get_prefs(file="debug_features_...xml"). This shows MANUAL OVERRIDES only, not effective flag state: debug_features_*.xml holds only flags the debug menu overrode, and an override is deleted once it matches the server value. A flag missing from this file can still be ON server-side -- absence means "no override," never "disabled." Prefer get_feature_flag/list_feature_flags/search_feature_flags for the actual live value; use this route only when the manual-override history itself is what is being asked about.
- "what did the app remember" / "what is cached in prefs" / "what team_prefs are set" -> list_prefs then get_prefs
- "save this" / "file this as a bug" / "share this" / "bundle this" / "attach to ticket" / "give me a repro" / "snapshot this" / "preserve this" / "hold this state" / "save what you just saw" -> capture_snapshot

Key behaviors:
- Network/RTM buffers clear on shutdown. Clogs persist from app start.
- If ping fails, do NOT retry. Tell the user and fall back to code-only analysis.
- Fetch details eagerly. When results reveal interesting events, get their detail immediately.
- RTM event types use subtypes when available (e.g. message_changed, not message).
- Use wait_for_events with idle_timeout_ms instead of polling loops.
- Use ping(timeout_minutes=N) to extend sessions. Monitor remaining_minutes proactively.
- ping reports which app/profile is bound (android_user_id, profile, package). The debug
  build can run on more than one user (personal=0, plus a work profile or secondary user),
  and only the first to bind the socket wins. If events seem to come from the wrong app, tell
  the user which profile is bound and use list_profiles + activate_for_user to switch.
- MULTIPLE DEVICES: with more than one device attached, enable fails and returns the list of
  attached serials. Retry _radar_session_enable with device_serial set to one of them. When the
  intent is unclear (you cannot tell which device the user means), ask which device before retrying;
  do not guess. The enable success response names the bound device via device_label, so confirm it
  matches what the user expected. The picked device applies to every tool for the whole session. Do
  not confuse this with profiles: profiles are separate users on ONE device (personal vs work), while
  devices are separate hardware.
- Screenshots default to 720px. Use full_res=true only when detail matters.
- Setup: /slack-radar-setup
- Manual enable (no skill): adb shell am broadcast -a slack.debug.ENABLE_RADAR --ei timeout_minutes 5 -p com.Slack.internal.debug
  Then: adb forward tcp:8099 localabstract:slack-radar (prefix adb -s <serial> when multiple devices are attached)

WEB DASHBOARD (/radar-ui):
A browser-based dashboard (http://localhost:8100) shows the same live device data as
tabs: Live (everything), Network, RTM, Clogs, Traces, and Logs, each with counters, a graph, a
filterable feed, and a payload inspector. Launched via the /radar-ui skill, which runs
`npx @slack/radar-mcp web` (a global install also exposes it as `slack-radar`).

PROACTIVELY offer the dashboard when it would help — do not wait to be asked. The moment a
device session turns visual or multi-step, say so and offer to open it, e.g.: "This is
easier to watch live — want me to open the Radar dashboard?" Offer (once per thread) when:
- User says "watch", "monitor", "let me see", "show me live" about device traffic
- User wants to share traffic with a colleague, pair, or teammate
- User is doing a multi-minute investigation and the transcript is getting noisy
- User explicitly asks about a GUI, UI, browser view, or dashboard

OFFER, then open ONLY AFTER THE USER AGREES — opening a browser window is a user-visible
action; never pop one unbidden. On a yes, run the /radar-ui skill (or tell them to run
`npx @slack/radar-mcp web`) and hand over the URL. Nudge, do not auto-open.
DO NOT offer for single-query debugging or when the user is happy reading results in the
transcript. Offer when visual inspection adds real value.

SCREEN OVERLAY (in the dashboard):
The dashboard has a '▣ Screen' button that mirrors the LIVE device screen in a side panel,
plus a full-resolution screenshot and screen recording. It is OFF by default and opens to a
consent notice first, because it shows real on-screen content (open DMs, messages). The live
mirror needs ffmpeg on the user's machine; the screenshot does not. If the user wants the live
screen and ffmpeg is missing, tell them plainly that live mirroring needs ffmpeg and give the
platform install command (mac: `brew install ffmpeg`; debian/ubuntu: `sudo apt install ffmpeg`;
windows: `winget install ffmpeg`), and note the screenshot works without it. NEVER run the
install for them. The dashboard's /health response reports screen.ffmpeg / screen.liveCast /
screen.installHint, so you can check before suggesting.

CUSTOM DASHBOARD (open_radar_dashboard):
The pre-built tabs (Live/Network/RTM/Clogs/Traces/Logs) cover the common cases. When the user
describes a live view the tabs do not show, SUGGEST building it; invoke open_radar_dashboard
only after they agree or explicitly ask for a custom view/dashboard (same discipline as
/radar-ui). To build, translate their words into a spec and call the tool; it renders your
spec as a 'Custom' tab on the dashboard (default http://localhost:8100) and returns the URL
for you to share. Cases worth suggesting it for:
- "graph calls per second vs average response time and flag the slow ones"
- "count every DM I receive and beep when one arrives"
- "show only RTM events on channel C... and let me click each for its payload"
- "watch network calls whose body contains <substring>"
Authoring rules:
- source is one of network/rtm/clog/trace/log/all ('all' = one unified timeline).
- match filters on SUMMARY fields only, by source: network=url/method/status_code,
  rtm=event_type/direction/channel, clog=event_name, trace=trace_name/span_name,
  log=tag/level/message/pid/package.
  NEVER invent a field; a match on a field the stream does not carry silently matches
  nothing. To filter on body text use bodyContains (network/all only), which fetches detail.
- viz composes counter/rate/sparkline/feed/inspector/graph. graph needs a series array
  (1-2 entries; metric ratePerSec/count/avg/errorRate; avg needs a field like duration_ms).
- highlight {field, op, value} flags rows breaching a numeric threshold; alert {sound,flash,
  say, at} fires on each live match (or once at the Nth). Author an honest one-line `summary`.
Calling it again replaces/refines the live custom dashboard. The dashboard reads a connected
device, so Radar must be armed to show data (it has its own Reconnect button). Debug builds
only; local only. Does not open a browser window for you; surface the returned URL to the user.

CAPTURE_SNAPSHOT OUTPUT:
When capture_snapshot returns, tell the user:
  1. The result.zip_path if non-null (the single shareable file). Fall back to
     result.path (a directory) if zip_path is null.
  2. A one-line summary of counts (network/rtm/clogs/traces/log_lines/screenshot).
  3. Print this EXACT sentence as the privacy line, verbatim — no paraphrase, no
     compression, no skipping even under time pressure:
     "Privacy: bundle.json contains raw API request/response bodies (including auth headers), RTM message content, user IDs, clog payloads, and performance trace spans. Review before sharing externally."
  4. If result.log_lines_truncated is true, say: 'you got fewer log lines than
     requested because the 1 MB read cap was the limiting factor.'
  5. If the user's original ask was 'file this as a bug' / 'attach to ticket' /
     similar, offer to attach result.zip_path via the Jira MCP or Slack MCP as
     the next step. Do NOT invoke the attach without asking. Just offer.
  6. If result.errors is non-empty, enumerate which parts failed so the user
     knows what is missing before they ship the bundle.
stderr: [radar] could not tell whether an Android device is attached (adb missing, slow, or failing), so defaulting to android. Pass --platform=webapp to target a webapp Radar instead.
